interaction_definition: J=(T_seed_scalar*T_adj_ExactS)/(T_seed_ExactS*T_adj_scalar)=(sharing speedup in seed order)/(sharing speedup in adjacent order). Four medians from the same graph, job and protocol.
interpretation_limits: J>1 is a descriptive positive multiplicative interaction, not a statistical significance result or proof of AVX-AMX execution overlap.
J sample bounds are cartesian min/max envelopes of observed samples, not confidence intervals or cross-machine guarantees.
ExactI has its own loop and metadata costs; ExactS/ExactI is a mechanism contrast, while ExactS/Scalar is the net benefit over the simpler same-order baseline.
At c=0, no source decode or current-index read is removed, so any speedup cannot be attributed to sharing.
Shared-edge incidence, edge addition order and projection counts are fixed across orders; timing interaction does not mean more sharing was found.
Plan copying and hashes are outside timing and alternating switch warmups are one per method. This is a causal-control steady-state protocol, not a per-inference deployment copy requirement.
No seed selection, synthetic/real pooling, cross-job timing denominator, or multiplication of speedups from separate protocols is used.
Repeated methods still execute at different times; node contention/frequency/thermal drift cannot be ruled out by bitwise/work gates.
A shared-node outlier is retained; its cause is not established. Generic PMU events do not identify a specific cache/TLB/MLP mechanism.

preserved_counterexample.interpretation: Consecutive control is unusually slow and variable. Preserve all points; do not treat its inflated ExactS/ExactI ratio as stable shared-decode speedup.
